$comment: Encodes the three licence buckets this project enforces automatically. This file is the diffable enforcement policy. Do not add a licence to permissive-prod without a written licensing review and the maintainer's approval — that is the whole point of this file being a human-diffed allow-list rather than an inference.
alwaysBlockedComment: Source-available USE-restricting licences. These condition on USE, not distribution, so the 'it's only a build tool' heuristic that clears a broad devDependencies bucket does not apply — checked in every bucket, including devDependencies. Matched as a case-insensitive substring of the licence string, since these often appear combined (e.g. 'Apache-2.0 WITH Commons-Clause').
admitsPackagesComment: Packages admitted by NAME and exact licence string, for bucket B only (a package a consumer installs, never one that is bundled into what a Nave package ships). They are not licence identifiers: neither CC-BY-4.0 nor LGPL-3.0-or-later is admitted in general, and prodPermissive is unchanged. A new platform build or a changed licence string on a listed name is not on this list and reds the gate. The rows are the fifteen approved by name for the packages that installing the next peer brings in; a row is only ever removed here, and one is added only with a new written approval.
prodPermissiveComment: Bucket B (dependencies/peerDependencies): permissive only auto-passes. Apache-2.0 is accepted but is NOT free — its NOTICE duty (§4(d)) becomes a real THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES obligation the moment anything under it is bundled (bucket A), which the no-inlined-dependency guard (packages/*/test/no-inlined-dependency.test.ts) is what keeps bucket A empty. Python-2.0 is accepted on the same terms: if anything under it were bundled, its notices would have to be kept and a brief summary of the changes included. Anything not on this list — including weak copyleft (MPL-2.0, LGPL) and strong copyleft (GPL, AGPL) — fails the gate and routes to the maintainer for a written licensing review before it can be added; a 'review item' is not an auto-pass, so it is not on this list until it has been reviewed by name, not by licence-family blanket.
prodPermissiveSchemaComment: Each entry carries only its own licence identifier (id), and the object shape is load-bearing rather than stylistic: check-license-allowlist.mjs matches a package's declared licence against entry.id, so a bare string here would silently match nothing, and check-license-enumeration-provenance.mjs rejects any entry that is not an object with a non-empty, already-trimmed id, so that cannot happen quietly.
